## Why This Is Asked

Tests the ability to design a robust, offline-first feature flag system with deterministic evaluation and safe rollback, critical in finance or enterprise apps.

## Key Concepts

- Deterministic feature rollouts using device-scoped hash
- Local persistence with Room/DataStore, and versioning
- Background syncing with WorkManager and backoff
- Dependency handling and sane defaults
- Rollback/audit trail and rollback safety

## Code Example

```kotlin
val rollout = 30
val deviceHash = hash(androidId + flagName)
val active = (deviceHash % 100) < rollout
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you handle changes to rollout percentages without causing mid-flight inconsistencies?
- How would you ensure security and integrity of flag updates from server (signatures, TLS pinning).

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This checks practical Android networking, simple architecture, and lifecycle safety for beginners.

## Key Concepts
- Retrofit service and data model
- Repository pattern with in-memory cache
- Kotlin coroutines with retry/backoff
- ViewModel and LiveData for UI state
- Basic test plan coverage

## Code Example
```kotlin
data class Post(val userId: Int, val id: Int, val title: String, val body: String)
interface PostsApi { suspend fun getPosts(): List<Post> }
class PostsRepository(private val api: PostsApi) {
  private var cache: List<Post>? = null
  suspend fun getPosts(): List<Post> {
    cache?.let { return it }
    val data = api.getPosts()
    cache = data
    return data
  }
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test network failures and backoff behavior?
- How would you ensure cancellation and avoid leaks in ViewModel?
